description: ODDs is the Occupancy Detection Dataset published by Simon Fraser University for evaluating household occupancy and sleep inference. It records power-meter readings, ambient light and temperature, with weather and daylight observations, at fifteen-minute intervals for about eight months. The provider states that it monitors the same home later used for AMPds, but it is a separate earlier collection. Harvard Dataverse supplies tab-delimited sensor tables, an equipment table and a SQL schema. The terms explicitly apply CC BY 4.0 and permit free reuse even though the API's structured licence field is empty. The own metadata does not identify exact start and end dates or establish a representative household sample. These observations can calibrate occupancy-driven demand and building digital-twin models, complementing data-eth-eco-electricity-consumption-occupancy. A caveat is that low-frequency signals can miss short activities, and measured light or power should not automatically be treated as ground-truth presence. The deposit documents occupancy-inference research, not a deployment-tested building control service.
